questions.q: According to this lesson, why can two sign-ins with identical correct credentials and a passing MFA challenge still represent different levels of risk?
options: The device each sign-in comes from can carry very different security posture, even though the identity signal looks the same in both
MFA challenges are always weaker on personal devices
Microsoft Entra ID assigns a different password strength score per device
Conditional Access cannot evaluate identity and device at the same time
questions.explain: A managed, encrypted, Intune-enrolled laptop and an unknown personal device carry very different risk even with identical, correctly authenticated credentials — which is why device compliance has to be evaluated alongside identity.

questions.q: Where do the granular rules that define an Intune compliance policy actually live?
options: In Microsoft Entra ID's Conditional Access policy editor directly
In Privileged Identity Management's role activation settings
In Intune, which evaluates the device and reports a simple compliant / not-compliant state to Microsoft Entra ID
In AWS IAM Identity Center's permission sets
questions.explain: Intune owns the detailed per-platform rules (OS version, encryption, PIN, jailbreak/root detection, threat level); Entra ID and Conditional Access only consume the resulting compliant/not-compliant signal.

questions.q: What does the 'Require device to be marked as compliant' Conditional Access grant control actually check?
options: Whether the device is domain-joined on-premises
Whether Intune currently considers the device healthy against policy, right now
Whether the user has completed security awareness training
Whether the device was purchased through a corporate procurement process
questions.explain: This control asks about present-day security posture as currently reported by Intune, which is a different question from where or how the device was provisioned.

questions.q: How does the lesson distinguish 'Require Hybrid Azure AD joined device' from 'Require device to be marked as compliant'?
options: They are two names for the exact same Conditional Access check
Hybrid join only applies to mobile devices, while compliance only applies to desktops
Compliance is evaluated once at provisioning and never again, while hybrid join is checked continuously
Hybrid join is about device provenance (where it came from, who provisioned it), while compliance is about its present-day security posture
questions.explain: A device can be hybrid Azure AD joined but no longer compliant — for example, if its disk encryption was later disabled — so treating the two as interchangeable is a design mistake the lesson calls out.

questions.q: Why does the lesson argue device compliance must be evaluated inside the access decision itself, rather than as a periodic, out-of-band IT audit?
options: Periodic audits are more accurate than real-time checks
Intune cannot report compliance state to Conditional Access at all
Compliance state has to be available at the exact moment access is requested so a non-compliant device can be blocked on that request, not flagged for later review
Conditional Access only runs once per calendar quarter
questions.explain: A signal that's only checked periodically and out of band is auditing after the fact, not verifying explicitly — compliance earns its place in the decision only when evaluated at request time, every time.
